How the tab draws a dial, and how it is read

Read to half a minor division

$lo,\ hi$
dial range of the gauge (tab data)
gauge unit
$s,\ d$
numbered (major) and minor division
gauge unit
$r,\ v$
your reading; the plant value when checked
gauge unit
$\tau,\ \rho$
absolute and relative tolerance of the rounds sheet
unit, –
$s=\min\{0.1,0.2,0.25,0.5,1,2,2.5,5,10,\dots\}\ \text{with}\ (hi-lo)/s\le 10$at most ten numbered divisions per dial
$d=s/5$five minor ticks between numbers
$|r-v|\approx d/2$the eye splits one division in half
$|r-v|\le\max(\tau,\ \rho\,|v|)$the sheet accepts this, against the live plant

Gauge

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Twelve stations, one 405 m walk, grade to F4 and back.
  • 42 local displays: 21 at grade, none on F1.
  • A local gauge shows the process, not the transmitter.
  • Read to half a minor division; compare with the sheet's tolerance.

Interactive · pick a normal position · HANDVALVES.json

Seventeen hand valves, three normal positions

Only NO valves move from the close-up; LO and LC carry a car seal and refuse.

Close-ups in the Visual plant 3D tab

Read the stem and the seal, not the label

Opening a close-up logs the valve as checked; NO valves can then be operated.

Interactive · try to move a locked valve

Why the locked valves are locked

The seal is visible in the field; what it protects is not.

A closed relief isolation removes a protection layer silently: no DCS signal shows a hand valve's position.

Interactive · click each valve to set it, then check

The batch line-up: 15 open, 2 locked closed

A line-up is walked valve by valve before the batch; the panel cannot confirm it.

Interactive · a generic block valve on a flow loop

What the panel shows first

The line-up prevents it; this is how a missed valve shows itself.

A shut valve on an idle line stays silent until the line is needed.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • 12 NO, 3 LO, 2 LC hand valves on R-101.
  • The stem shows open or closed; the car seal shows locked.
  • LO valves keep the relief and the short-stop paths open.
  • A wrong valve may stay silent until its line is needed.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The rounds sheet grades against the plant at Check.
  • Identification passes at 90 % over the stations tried.
  • Only logged reads, checks and arrivals count.
  • Field checks open with the upset and grade out of 5.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the twelve stations in order; open a close-up for every reading.

2

Treat a local gauge as a second opinion on the transmitter.

3

Read to half a minor division and report against the tolerance.

4

Walk the line-up valve by valve; never break a car seal without a permit.

5

Expect a wrong valve to stay silent until its line is needed.
